scope: Original minimal asynchronous Engine/storage contract experiment; not reference Engine port, DSH integration, PostgreSQL, remote device, or production backend acceptance.

cases.name: N1 sync-style RELEASE before async callback settles
cases.detail: Late rejection leaves committed state: invariant violation reproduced.

cases.name: N2 transaction-local microtask dispatch leaks uncommitted effect
cases.detail: Handler ran once although durable state/effect rolled back.

cases.name: N3 enqueue only after state commit loses effect on process death
cases.detail: Actual child process terminated after state commit, before separate enqueue.

cases.name: P1 failures after state, after effect, and before commit roll back everything
cases.detail: All three failure windows: no state, intent, receipt, or wake.

cases.name: P2 independent reader sees no partial transaction across await
cases.detail: WAL reader standing in for a dispatcher stays responsive and sees only committed rows; no real dispatcher was run.

cases.name: P3 process death before-commit
cases.detail: Uncommitted state/intent/receipt all absent on fresh connection.

cases.name: P3 process death after-commit
cases.detail: Committed intent recovered by scan without wake; same command ID replayed without duplicate enqueue.

cases.name: P4 two Engine connections serialize concurrent read-await-write commands
P5 concurrent duplicate command IDs deduplicate; changed payload is rejected
cases.detail: One durable receipt and enqueue; command identity binds canonical input.

cases.name: P6 old success/failure/defer cannot change a revised effect
cases.detail: Stable queue position, new generation, no stale deletion/backoff/defer.

cases.name: P7 delete/re-enqueue protects against same-key generation ABA
cases.detail: New monotonic row incarnation prevents generation reuse from accepting stale completion.

cases.name: P8 replaced Assignment and human stop reject late domain callbacks
cases.detail: Effect settlement and domain callback fencing are separate checks; no claim that remote execution has stopped.

cases.name: P9 failed post-commit wake cannot turn durable success into rollback
cases.detail: Wake is an optimization; startup/periodic scan recovers committed intent.

cases.name: P10 leaked transaction capability is rejected after commit
cases.detail: No shared transaction/depth field; nested UoW rejects immediately instead of waiting on its own connection queue.

cases.name: P11 snapshot plus small-model revision CAS detects and replays conflict
cases.detail: Viable small-model alternative; does not prove cross-aggregate snapshot completeness or safe replay of full reference rules.

cases.name: P12 read-only storage rejects command without dispatch
cases.detail: Read-only storage fault causes no accepted durable state and no wake; not a network-partition experiment.
